goal: DEPTH: sub-sections / config sections in real integration with the backend — raise real coverage and capability levels
must_build: Every page in ui-spec/azure/cosmos.json (40 pages; nav: Overview, Activity log, Access control (IAM), Tags, Diagnose and solve problems, Cost Management, Quick start, Notifications, Data Explorer, Settings, Containers, Integrations, Monitoring, Automation)
Backend: ARM databaseAccounts + Cosmos data plane (test_azure_cosmos_core.py): accounts, Data Explorer (databases, containers, items, query), keys
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/azure/cosmos.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Capability feature ids MUST start with 'azure.' (e.g. 'azure.cosmos.<section>') — ids share one namespace with the AWS registry
Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape
note:
DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:
  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.
  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.

depth_targets.title: SQL query (SELECT) over the Cosmos data plane
limitations: Covers a pragmatic SELECT subset (projection, a single WHERE comparison/IN predicate, ORDER BY); joins, subqueries, aggregate/system functions and stored procedures are not implemented.

depth_targets.title: Default consistency level
limitations: properties.consistencyPolicy.defaultConsistencyLevel round-trips through ARM, but every data-plane read in Vyomi is already strongly consistent regardless of the configured level.

depth_targets.title: Replicate data globally (region list, failover)
limitations: properties.locations round-trips through ARM, but Vyomi has one logical region: added regions are not separately provisioned, and Manual/Service-Managed Failover do not move the data plane anywhere.

depth_targets.title: Backup & Restore policy
limitations: properties.backupPolicy round-trips through ARM exactly as configured at create time, but Vyomi never takes or restores a backup.

depth_targets.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered ARM mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

depth_targets.title: Access control (IAM): role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), but the generic ARM list is subscription-wide (not scoped to this one account), and 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation is not modelled — Vyomi never denies a console action based on a role assignment.
